title: Savoir, connaître et voir au présent
summary: Recognise facts, familiarity and perception while forming three common irregular families.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Knowing a fact or being familiar
paragraphs: Conjugation means changing a verb to match its subject and tense. `Savoir` introduces a fact or a skill with an infinitive, the dictionary form of a verb. `Connaître` introduces familiarity with a person, place or thing. Their present forms must be learned separately; the `nous` stem helps with other plural forms.
points: `Savoir`: `je sais, tu sais, il/elle/on sait, nous savons, vous savez, ils/elles savent`.
`Connaître`: `je connais, tu connais, il/elle/on connaît, nous connaissons, vous connaissez, ils/elles connaissent`. `Reconnaître` adds `re-` to each form.
The traditional circumflex in `connaît/paraît/disparaît` is retained here; 1990 spellings `connait/parait/disparait` are also accepted.

examples.english: Do you know how to drive?

sections.title: Appearing and seeing
paragraphs: `Paraître` means 'to seem' or 'to appear/be published'. It shares the `-aître` pattern with `connaître`. `Apparaître` and `disparaître` follow `paraître` in the present. `Voir` changes to `voy-` for `nous` and `vous`, but uses `voi-` elsewhere. `Revoir` follows it. `Prévoir` also follows these present endings, though its other tenses need separate attention.
points: `Paraître`: `je parais, tu parais, il/elle/on paraît, nous paraissons, vous paraissez, ils/elles paraissent`.
`Voir`: `je vois, tu vois, il/elle/on voit, nous voyons, vous voyez, ils/elles voient`.

examples.english: The results appear on the screen.
We can see the bridge from here.
examples.note: English can is natural in perception; French uses `voyons`.

examples.english: They are seeing their colleagues again on Monday.
examples.note: No `y` in this third-person plural form.

sections.title: Transfer a pattern without guessing from the last letters
paragraphs: The present pattern of `voir` extends to `entrevoir` (glimpse) and `pourvoir` (provide for): `nous entrevoyons, ils entrevoient`; `nous pourvoyons, ils pourvoient`. `Recevoir` belongs to a different family despite its final letters.

`Fuir` (flee or avoid) has the same `i/y` distribution as `voir` but its own `fu-` base. `Naître` (be born) uses `nais-/naiss-`; `renaître` (be reborn) keeps those forms with `re-`. `Méconnaître` (fail to recognise or know adequately) and `comparaître` (appear in court) preserve the `connaître/paraître` endings.
points: `Fuir`: `je fuis, tu fuis, il/elle/on fuit, nous fuyons, vous fuyez, ils/elles fuient`.
`Naître`: `je nais, tu nais, il/elle/on naît, nous naissons, vous naissez, ils/elles naissent`. `Nait` is also accepted under the 1990 spelling recommendations.

examples.note: `Fuir` need not describe physically running away.

examples.french: Les premières idées **naissent** pendant la discussion.
examples.english: The first ideas emerge during the discussion.
examples.note: `Naître` can be used figuratively; the plural has double `s`.

examples.french: Nous **entrevoyons** une solution, mais nous ne la connaissons pas encore en détail.
examples.english: We can glimpse a solution, but we do not yet know it in detail.

practice.prompt: Present of connaître: Elle ___ le directeur.
Present of voir: Vous ___ la différence.
Present of paraître: Ces chaussures ___ solides.
Present of savoir: Nous ___ réparer ce modèle.
Present of connaître: Tu ___ ce chemin.
Present of reconnaître: Les enfants ___ la chanson.
Present of disparaître: Le message ___ après dix secondes.
practice.explanation: Both spellings represent the singular form.

practice.prompt: Present of voir: Nous ___ un autre problème.
Present of revoir: Elle ___ sa famille ce soir.
Present of savoir: Les agents ___ où aller.
Present of prévoir: Je ___ une pause.
Present of connaître: Vous ___ nos tarifs.
Correct the verb only: Ils voyent la mer.
Present of apparaître: Une icône ___ ici.
Present of savoir: On ___ déjà la réponse.
practice.explanation: On takes the same form as il.

practice.prompt: Change only the subject and verb from Nous to Ils: Nous fuyons la foule.
practice.explanation: Fuir has y with nous/vous but i with ils/elles.

practice.prompt: Use naître in the present for an emerging idea: Une nouvelle question ___ de cette découverte.
practice.explanation: The singular form is naît, also written nait under the 1990 recommendations.

practice.prompt: Supply comparaître in the present: Demain, vous ___ devant le juge.
practice.explanation: The present can refer to a scheduled future event; comparaître keeps the paraître-family -aiss- plural stem.

production_task.prompt: A new colleague asks for help finding a room. Explain what you know, what you can see and whether you know the building.
production_task.model_answer: Je connais bien le bâtiment. Je sais où se trouve la salle, mais je ne vois pas son numéro d'ici. Nous voyons l'escalier à gauche : la salle est juste derrière.
production_task.translation: I know the building well. I know where the room is, but I cannot see its number from here. We can see the stairs on the left: the room is just behind them.
